first.rationale: Referral incentives have the strongest direct evidence of qualified revenue without retention harm, aligning best with sustainable long-term value. Verify that result and compare it with onboarding simplification given the current completion decline. Avoid reacting to competitor pricing with promotions because prior gains came with materially worse 30-day retention. Limit eligibility to established customers and monitor revenue quality and retention.

final.rationale: Run a referral-incentive experiment limited to established accounts older than six months. The verified source showed a 7% lift in qualified revenue, 21% more referral starts, and no retention tradeoff, directly supporting sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Shorter onboarding is validated and relevant to the current completion decline, but its source record does not establish a qualified-revenue lift. Promotional pricing is rejected because its known retention damage conflicts with the primary objective. Measure referred-account quality and retention before considering broader exposure.
